Crown browse by type volume/amplification amplification treble booster browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Crown Fuzz and Treble Booster Published on April 6, 2020 Crown fuzz treble boost pedal Information The Crown Fuzz and Treble Booster is an early version of Applied Audio Products Inc.'s classic two-in-one fuzz and high-frequency boost design, manufactured in New Jersey during the late 1960s. Sold under multiple brand names including Goya, Giulietti, Sano, and Lou Rose, the Crown version represents one of the first commercially distributed OEM examples of this circuit. It combines a transistor-based fuzz effect with an independent treble booster, offering players the option of thick, saturated fuzz tones or bright, cutting lead sounds in a single compact pedal. The fuzz section produces a gritty, aggressive distortion with strong midrange and harmonic texture, while the treble booster enhances clarity and bite, particularly effective for rhythm work or for driving amplifiers into natural overdrive. The two effects can be used individually or together, providing a wide tonal range characteristic of early American fuzz pedals. Built with handwired, point-to-point construction and featuring heavy-duty metal housing, the Crown Fuzz and Treble Booster reflects the robust build quality of Applied Audio's designs. Early examples include an oversized battery test lamp and on/off pot for the treble circuit, both features that appeared on the earliest Goya and Lou Rose models. The control layout and component choice mirror those of other Applied Audio units, confirming a shared production lineage and marking this as one of the earliest iterations of the company's signature fuzz platform. Controls Volume : Adjusts the overall output level Fuzz : Controls the intensity and gain of the fuzz effect Treble : Sets the amount of high-frequency boost Battery Test Button : Activates the indicator lamp to check battery charge Fuzz Switch : Engages or disables the fuzz circuit Treble Switch : Engages or disables the treble boost circuit Connections Input Jack : 1/4 inch mono Output Jack : 1/4 inch mono Technical Specifications Circuit Type : Analog fuzz and treble booster combination Transistors : Germanium (early production) or earl
